texts.preamble: Anirudh Banerjee vs The State Of Jharkhand And Ors on 6 January, 2017 Author: Rongon Mukhopadhyay Bench: Rongon Mukhopadhyay In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi W. P. (Cr.) No. 385 of 2016 --- Anirudh Banerjee ... ... Petitioner Versus State of Jharkhand & Ors. ... ... Respondents --- Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rongon Mukhopadhyay --- For the Petitioner : Mr. Indrajit Sinha, Advocate For the Respondents : Mr. Rajiv Ranjan Mishra, G. P. - Ii --- 02/06.01.2017 It
texts.arguments: has been submitted by Mr. Indrajit Sinha, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, that precursor to invocation of Section 52 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is following the principle as laid down in Section 49 of the Act but the adjudicating authority had not considered Section 49 of the Act. It has also been submitted that the petitioner has not been given proper opportunity to defend his case as in terms of the Rules 3.1.1(8) the Adjudicating Officer was supposed to intimate the person who was proceeded against or his authorized representative with respect to the offence alleged to have been committed by such person and indicating the provisions of the Act, rules and regulations in support of which the contravention is alleged to have taken place. Learned counsel has also referred to Sub-rule 9 of Rule 3.1.1 which envisages that such person who has been proceeded against has to be given an opportunity to produce such documents or evidence which is relevant for the purpose of the case. It has thus been submitted that the basic tenets of the proceeding against the petitioner under the Act was not followed and in such circumstance, therefore, the impugned order dated 04.10.2016 passed by the Adjudicating Officer-cum- Deputy Commissioner, Dhanbad in Food Safety and Standards Case No. 07 of 2016 deserves to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK]. At this, Mr. Rajiv Ranjan Mishra, learned G. P. - II, submits that he has to take instruction and file a counter affidavit.
